n1.text: King Kenny is standing before the big clock in {kingHall}, hands on his hips. It has stopped at ten past four. "My friends arrive this afternoon," he says, "and I would like the clock going. You look like someone who can help."

choices.label: Ask Jack to take a look

n2.text: Jack wipes his hands on a rag and listens carefully. "Stopped clocks usually want two things," he says. "A little oil and a proper winding." He pats his toolbox. "I've the tools, but the oil is running low."

choices.label: Fetch clock oil from the shop

n3.text: Queen Rose looks up from her tea and smiles. "Ah. I think Robin borrowed the winding key last week for a magic trick. Knowing Robin, it may have vanished on purpose." She pours you a cup while you think.

n4.text: You open the little door in the clock's case. A folded napkin is wedged beside the pendulum. You ease it out, and the pendulum begins to swing. Tick, tock. The King beams, though the chime stays silent.

choices.label: Enjoy the ticking with the King

n5.text: Jack works quietly, putting a drop of oil here and a gentle turn there. The King hovers and offers advice nobody needs. At last Jack winds the spring with his spare key, and the pendulum swings. Tick. Tock.

choices.label: Set the hands with the King

n6.text: Among the shelves of string, soap and spare buttons, you find a small tin of clock oil. The person at the counter wraps it in paper and slips a peppermint into your hand. "For the journey back," they say.

n7.text: Robin throws open the door of {jokerCaravan} with a flourish. "A key? Of course!" Robin plucks it from behind your ear. "But first, a riddle. What has hands but cannot clap?"

n8.text: {bakery} smells of warm bread and butter. You buy a bag of fresh rolls for the King's guests. "A stopped clock is only time stopping for tea," says the person at the counter, handing you the bag.

n9.text: Together you and the King nudge the hands round to the right time. Jack closes the little door with a click. When the friends arrive, the clock is ticking steadily, and nobody guesses it was ever stopped. It was a good afternoon.

n10.text: You wait, and on the hour the clock gives a deep, golden chime that fills {kingHall}. The King laughs out loud and shakes Jack's hand, then yours. His friends arrive to the sound of it, and he looks very proud.

n11.text: Robin declares your answer "nearly magical" and hands over the key with a bow. Back in {kingHall}, the King takes it, opens the clock and winds it with great ceremony. The clock ticks. Robin pretends to have planned all of it.

n12.text: You sit beside the King and listen to the clock tick. "I never noticed how much I missed that," he says. The chime can wait for another day. When his friends arrive, they all agree it is a calm, friendly sound.

n13.text: The clock strikes, a little late but very sure of itself. Robin takes a bow as though it were part of the act, and the King laughs. When his friends arrive, you are all sharing warm rolls under the ticking clock.
